`pipeline-test` is the contract test piece (PF-009): one `BAKED_` bench, one `PBR_` cube with a normal map, one `SHADER_test_grid` panel with the `Col` mask, one `GLOW_` strip, `ANCHOR_shared`, two `HOTSPOT_`s, one `GLOW_` accent, four `INST_pin_` copies of `shared_pin`, and the two-second clip `shared_test_cube_rise` (Blender report: `Blender Assets/shared/REPORT-pipeline-test.md`, approved by the owner). Only the dev route `/dev/assets` loads it. Like everything in `public/`, its files are reachable on the live domain even though no production page uses them (accepted for this test piece).

## Site assets from Blender (PF-009)

### Adding an asset, step by step

1. **Blender.** The Blender chat exports the approved piece to `Blender Assets/<chapter>/export/<slug>.glb` under the asset contract (STANDARDS.md §6, BLENDER.md §4): `.glb`, +Y up, metres, transforms applied, no compression, no cameras or lights, names by prefix. `<chapter>` is a scroll chapter (`port`, `bus`, `memory`, `array`, `core`, `uplink`) or `shared`; `<slug>` is lower-case words joined by hyphens.
2. **Budget.** If the asset needs its own limits, add an entry under `assets.slugs["<chapter>/<slug>"]` in `budgets.config.mjs` (owner decision; otherwise the chapter limits apply).
3. **Pipeline.** `npm run asset -- <chapter>/<slug>` (needs KTX-Software's `ktx` on PATH, below). Add `--review <ID>` to write texture comparisons into `.review/<ID>/`.
4. **Check.** `npm test` (the manifest test checks every listed file's size and SHA-256), then `npm run size`.
5. **Commit** `public/assets/<chapter>/<slug>/`, `src/lib/journey/assets/manifest.generated.ts` and this file together. Raw exports never enter the repo.

A new `SHADER_<name>` needs its shader registered first (`src/components/journey/assets/shaders/library.ts` and `src/lib/journey/assets/shader-names.ts`); the pipeline warns loudly about an unknown name and the site draws a fallback.

### What the pipeline does (`scripts/asset.mjs`, `scripts/lib/asset/`)

It only reads the assets folder. Every step works in memory or in a temporary folder; the asset's folder, the manifest and this table are written only after every step has succeeded. On any failure it prints every problem and exits with code 1, having written nothing.

1. **Contract check** (`contract.mjs`; the name rules are shared with the site: `src/lib/journey/assets/contract-rules.ts`). Every violation is listed at once:
   - material names `BAKED_` / `PBR_` / `SHADER_` / `GLOW_` + lower-case words; a `BAKED_` material needs its base-colour image, a `GLOW_` one an emission colour;
   - mesh objects and mesh data `<chapter>_<element>[_<part>]` in lower case;
   - empties `ANCHOR_<chapter>`, `HOTSPOT_<name>`, `INST_<prop>_<nnn>`, `GLOW_<name>`; names unique;
   - every `INST_<prop>_*` has its source mesh `<chapter>_<prop>`, at the origin;
   - clips `<object>_<verb>`, the object being the node the clip animates;
   - scale 1 everywhere; mesh and parent nodes unrotated (transforms applied, +Y up – only empties may carry a rotation);
   - no cameras, no lights, no extensions in the raw file; images PNG with power-of-two sides.
   An unknown `SHADER_` name is a loud warning, not a failure.
2. **Budgets** (`budget.mjs`, `budgets.config.mjs` → `assets`): the slug's limits, else the chapter's (STANDARDS.md §3). Input: triangles drawn (an instanced prop once per copy), materials, images (count and sizes, largest first), objects, clips. Output: the largest texture side per tier (2048 high, 1024 low) and the chapter's download per tier (this asset plus the chapter's other assets in the manifest: ≤ 2 MB high, ≤ 1 MB low). `pipeline-test`: ≤ 5 000 triangles, 4 materials, 2 images (1024 and 512), 13 objects, 1 clip.
3. **Clean-up** (`geometry.mjs`): dedup (named properties are never merged), prune (empties, extras and the UVs of untextured surfaces kept), `TANGENT` removed from primitives whose material has no normal map. Nothing is flattened or joined.
4. **Geometry**: Meshopt (`EXT_meshopt_compression` + `KHR_mesh_quantization`, level high: positions 14 bit, normals 8 bit, UVs 12 bit, colours 8 bit). Quantization moves each mesh into a unit grid and puts the inverse scale and offset on its node; for an animated node it adds an unnamed child node holding the mesh, so the clip still drives the named node. The loaders account for both.
5. **Textures** (`textures.mjs`, KTX2 / `KHR_texture_basisu` through `ktx create`): images are first normalised to plain 8-bit PNGs with exactly the stored pixel values (embedded colour profiles ignored, checked pixel for pixel). Normal maps: UASTC + Zstandard, linear. Colour images (base colour, bake, emission): encoded as both ETC1S and UASTC, sRGB; ETC1S is kept only when its level-0 SSIM is ≥ 0.995 in every channel, otherwise UASTC (`settings.mjs`: on the pipeline-test bake ETC1S bands the dark gradients into green/blue contours – SSIM 0.983 although its PSNR is 53.6 dB). Other data textures: UASTC + Zstandard, linear. Full mip chains.
6. **Variants**: `public/assets/<chapter>/<slug>/<slug>-high.glb` (full-size textures) and `-low.glb` (textures at half size; geometry unchanged unless the slug's budget entry sets `lowSimplify`). Each variant is read back and must still carry the same materials, empties, instances, clips and triangle count.
7. **Manifest**: `src/lib/journey/assets/manifest.generated.ts` (typed, imported by the site: key, chapter, slug, source file with size and SHA-256, date, licence, triangles, objects, materials and kinds, textures with codec and per-tier size, clips, empties by prefix, instances, files per tier with bytes and SHA-256, tool versions) and the table at the top of this file.

**Deterministic.** The same export gives byte-identical files (unit-tested, and run twice on `pipeline-test`). The date stays while the source's SHA-256 is unchanged. KTX-Software's UASTC rate-distortion optimisation is not bit-exact from run to run (measured: about one encode in sixteen of the bake differed by 16 bytes in level 0, even with `--threads 1 --uastc-rdo-m`), so an image whose pixels and encoder settings are unchanged keeps the encoding already published (`pixelSha256` and `encodingKey` in the manifest; only files whose SHA-256 still matches are reused). A changed image or setting is encoded afresh.

**The KTX tool (D-43).** KTX-Software v4.4.2, the stable release (Apache-2.0), installed on the machine with `ktx` on PATH (Windows: `C:\Program Files\KTX-Software\bin`; a terminal opened before the install needs restarting). `KTX_BIN` may point at the executable instead. The pipeline refuses a missing tool, a pre-release (e.g. v5.0.0-rc2) and anything older than v4.3. It is not an npm package: CI has no `ktx`, so the KTX2 unit tests are skipped there (and say so); pipeline runs happen on the owner's machine.

### Tier variants

| Tier | Loads |
|---|---|
| high, medium | `<slug>-high.glb` |
| low | `<slug>-low.glb` |
| static | nothing |

`variantForTier` in `src/lib/journey/assets/manifest.ts`.

### Decoders served by the site

`npm run decoders` (`scripts/copy-decoders.mjs`, run by `prebuild` and `predev`) copies from the installed three.js into `public/decoders/three-r<REVISION>/` (git-ignored, regenerated on every build): `basis/basis_transcoder.js` and `basis/basis_transcoder.wasm` (Basis Universal, for KTX2), `meshopt_decoder.module.js` (Meshopt; its WASM is embedded in the file). The site asks for `/decoders/three-r${REVISION}/` with `REVISION` imported from the same three.js, so the files always match the code. A build without the 3D layer (the production deployment, D-39) removes the folder: the live site serves no decoder.

| File (three r187, measured by `npm run size`, PF-009) | Raw | gzip | Brotli |
|---|---|---|---|
| `basis/basis_transcoder.js` | 57.5 KB | 15.2 KB | 13.7 KB |
| `basis/basis_transcoder.wasm` | 527.3 KB | 247.6 KB | 203.6 KB |
| `meshopt_decoder.module.js` | 29.3 KB | 7.8 KB | 6.9 KB |

They are downloaded once per visit, on the first asset load, and count towards the interactive hero's download budget (STANDARDS §3, ≤ 3 MB high · ≤ 2 MB low) once PF-010 loads the Port's assets.

## Journey camera path – stand-in (PF-008)

**Code-generated, not a Blender asset.** Plumbing for the camera rig until PF-010 exports the real path from Blender into the same two files (the asset contract, STANDARDS §6). Replacing them needs no code change (`src/components/journey/scene/path-swap.test.ts`, `e2e/scroll.spec.ts`). Written by `npm run path:standin` (`scripts/make-standin-path.mjs`, generator in `scripts/lib/standin-path.mjs`); the unit test fails if the committed files differ from the generator's output. Served from one fixed folder, `public/assets/world/` (`JOURNEY_PATH_DIR` in `src/components/journey/scene/path-asset.ts`; PF-009 kept it there: the path is not a chapter asset and is not processed by the asset pipeline, whose output goes to `public/assets/<chapter>/<slug>/`). Fetched only by the lazy journey chunks (non-static tiers on `/`); the static tier and the production deployment never request it.

| Slug | File | Date | Contents | Bytes in repo (raw = served, uncompressed) | Licence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `world-path` | `public/assets/world/world-path.glb` | 2026-11-25 | glTF 2.0 binary: one node `CAM_journey` with a perspective camera (vertical FOV 35°, near 0.1 m, far 200 m) and the animation clip `journey` – translation and rotation, LINEAR, a key on every frame, 361 keys (30 fps, frames 1–361, 12 s, first key at 0 s). No meshes, no textures, 0 triangles | 12 828 | © Swapnil Raj (generated by the repo's code) |
| `world-path` (markers) | `public/assets/world/world-path.json` | 2026-11-25 | `{ fps: 30, firstFrame: 1, lastFrame: 361, markers: { CH_port: 1, CH_bus: 55, CH_memory: 115, CH_array: 175, CH_core: 245, CH_uplink: 305 } }` – unevenly spaced on purpose, so the rig is seen to follow the markers rather than even spacing | 195 | © Swapnil Raj (generated) |

The glide: from PF-007's camera pose (0, 0, 8) looking down −Z, 48 m forward with a gentle drift left, a rise of 0.9 m, a yaw of ±0.14 rad and a bank of ±0.03 rad. The six stand-in marker pillars are not in the file: `scene/standin-markers.tsx` places one per chapter from the path itself (ahead of and to the right of each chapter's start pose; one instanced mesh, unlit `surface-raised`, 6 × 12 triangles).

## Stage 1 stills and icons (PF-028)

Blender renders approved by the owner (`Blender Assets/stills/`, REPORT-stills.md runs 1 and 2), encoded by `npm run media:stills` (`scripts/encode-stills.mjs`, sharp from the Next.js install). The script only reads the assets folder. It writes the files below and fails without writing anything if a source has the wrong size, or if a still served by next/image at its largest size would exceed 250 KB.

- **Stills** are WebP masters at full resolution (lossy, quality 90, effort 6, smart subsampling; mean difference to the PNG 0.7–1.2 / 255). The site never serves a master as it is: next/image resizes each one per device and re-encodes it (AVIF, else WebP, quality 75). The stills are drawn full-bleed, so the largest variant is the master's own width, because next/image never enlarges. "Largest served" is that variant, measured from the running build by `npm run size`.
- **Social background**: `still-social.png` downscaled to 1200 × 630 JPEG (quality 90, mozjpeg). next/og reads PNG or JPEG, not WebP.
- **Icons** are made from `icon-mark-transparent.png` (favicon, trimmed to the mark so it fills 16 px) and `icon-mark.png` (the mark on #07090C: app icons and the apple-touch icon), using Lanczos downscaling.

Date of all files: 2026-11-24.

Stills files live in `public/media/stills/`. Their sizes and paths are in the content data (`src/content/data/stills.ts`), and `next build` checks them against the files. To replace a still: render it in Blender, run `npm run media:stills`, then `npm test`. The contrast test samples the new file. Then `npm run size`.

Not used: `icon-mark-64.png` (the favicon is made from the 1024 px transparent mark).
